head_commit.message:
fix(18): LLAMA_BUILD_APP defaults ON and built a CLI whose deps we had disabled

The pin took, and it took visibly:

    llama.cpp pinned: 3018a11e79e489b657dbb77c95694889ccff92df
    header has llama_get_memory
    header has llama_memory_clear
    -- ggml commit:  3018a11

So the 11 API errors are resolved -- the header assertions now pass at configure
time instead of the wrapper failing to compile twenty minutes later.

The first build at the new pin failed differently:

    FAILED: [code=1] bin/llama
    ld: error: unable to find library -lllama-server-impl
    ld: error: unable to find library -lllama-cli-impl
    clang++: error: linker command failed with exit code 1

THE OPTION THAT WAS MISSING

At 3018a11e7 the top-level CMakeLists.txt declares:

    option(LLAMA_BUILD_APP "llama: build the unified binary" ${LLAMA_STANDALONE})

${LLAMA_STANDALONE} is ON for a standalone build, so LLAMA_BUILD_APP is ON by
default. The flags passed here set TESTS, EXAMPLES and SERVER to OFF but never
mentioned APP -- so pinning the desktop commit switched on a target the previously
pinned branch did not have. The unified binary links llama-server-impl and
llama-cli-impl, and EXAMPLES/SERVER being OFF is exactly what removed those, so
bin/llama was assembled with its own dependencies switched out from under it.

Two more are ON by default at this commit and equally unnecessary here:

    option(LLAMA_BUILD_COMMON "llama: build common utils library" ${LLAMA_STANDALONE})
    option(LLAMA_BUILD_UI     "llama: build the embedded Web UI for server"     ON)

Added: -DLLAMA_BUILD_APP=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_COMMON=OFF -DLLAMA_BUILD_UI=OFF

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE LINK ERROR

build.rs links EVERY .a the package ships (crates/gs-ffi/build.rs:200 walks lib/
and links each stem it finds). So leaving a CLI in dist/lib/ would not merely cost
disk -- rustc would be handed it as a link input. The package needs to contain
libraries and nothing else.

Nothing in this stack wants a CLI, a server, or the common utils: the wrapper
calls llama_* and ggml_* APIs only, which is why the only errors it produced were
about those two namespaces.

head_commit.message:
fix(17): pin android-deps to the DESKTOP llama.cpp commit — the API versions disagreed

android-deps.yml:398 cloned llama.cpp at a moving branch:

    git clone --depth 1 --branch b4581 .../llama.cpp.git

b4581 is b636228c0ad0db95bf73008094c6145a05615cf6. The desktop build does not use
that. .cargo/config.toml:37 points GS_LLAMA_ROOT at
/mnt/new_volume/llm-workspace/llama.cpp, whose HEAD is
3018a11e79e489b657dbb77c95694889ccff92df (2026-07-29), and
native/cpp/llama_wrapper/llama_wrapper.cpp is written against THAT version.

So the two builds compiled the same wrapper against two different APIs. Run
36460210545 was the first time the wrapper was ever compiled for Android, and
the disagreement is the whole of its output:

    error: use of undeclared identifier 'llama_get_memory'
           did you mean 'llama_get_model'?
    error: use of undeclared identifier 'llama_memory_clear'
    error: use of undeclared identifier 'llama_memory_seq_pos_max'
           did you mean 'llama_kv_cache_seq_pos_max'?
    error: use of undeclared identifier 'GGML_BACKEND_DEVICE_TYPE_IGPU'
    error: cannot initialize a parameter of type 'struct llama_context *'
           with an rvalue of type 'const struct llama_model *'
    11 errors generated.

CONFIRMED AT THE HEADER LEVEL, NOT INFERRED FROM THE ERRORS

Counting the symbols the wrapper needs in each tree's include/llama.h:

    3018a11e79e489b657dbb77c95694889ccff92df  ->  4 matches
    b636228c0ad0db95bf73008094c6145a05615cf6  ->  0 matches

GGML_BACKEND_DEVICE_TYPE_IGPU is likewise present at 3018a11e7 in
ggml/include/ggml-backend.h. So the desktop commit has every API the wrapper
uses and the pinned branch has none of them.

A SHALLOW CLONE CANNOT TAKE `--branch <sha>`, so the commit is fetched directly:

    git init -q src-llama
    git remote add origin https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp.git
    git fetch -q --depth 1 origin "$LLAMA_SHA"
    git checkout -q --detach FETCH_HEAD
    git submodule update --init --recursive || true

--recurse-submodules is a NO-OP at this commit: there is no .gitmodules and
git ls-tree shows ggml as an in-tree tree, not a 160000 gitlink. It is kept
because it costs nothing, and because ggml was a submodule historically — if that
ever changes back, without it this step would build against an empty directory
and fail obscurely.

THE PIN IS ASSERTED TWICE

A wrong checkout produces the same 11 errors twenty minutes later in a different
job, so the step checks both facts up front:

    [ "$GOT" != "$LLAMA_SHA" ] && exit 1
    grep -q llama_get_memory        src-llama/include/llama.h           || exit 1
    grep -q llama_memory_clear      src-llama/include/llama.h           || exit 1
    grep -q llama_memory_seq_pos_max src-llama/include/llama.h          || exit 1
    grep -q GGML_BACKEND_DEVICE_TYPE_IGPU src-llama/ggml/include/ggml-backend.h || exit 1

Header layout is unchanged and already correct: dist/include/ from
src-llama/include/, dist/ggml-include/ from src-llama/ggml/include/.

head_commit.message:
fix(16): the ggml headers are at ggml-include/, not ggml/include/ — first real link attempt

Blocker 1 is fixed. The documented path worked:

    NDK       : /home/runner/android-sdk/ndk/25.2.9519653
    sysroot   : .../sysroot/usr/lib
    companion : .../sysroot/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-android/libc++_shared.so

and the build moved past it to the first time it has ever attempted to compile
llama_wrapper.cpp for Android. That surfaced the next failure, and it is the real
one:

    native/prebuilts/android-x86_64/include/llama.h:4:10: fatal error:
      'ggml.h' file not found
    1 error generated.
    error occurred in cc-rs: command did not execute successfully
    ##[error]Process completed with exit code 101.

TWO LAYOUTS, AND build.rs GUESSED ONE

    .include(root.join("include"))
    .include(root.join("ggml").join("include"))   // build TREE: correct on desktop

    prebuilts/android-x86_64/ggml-include/ggml-alloc.h
    prebuilts/android-x86_64/ggml-include/ggml-backend.h
    ...                                    // PACKAGE: what mobile actually gets

GS_LLAMA_ROOT is a llama.cpp build tree and ggml headers live at ggml/include/.
GS_LLAMA_PREBUILT is the android-deps package and they live at ggml-include/.
The old code only added the build-tree path, so it had never been exercised on
mobile -- because until this run, nothing set GS_LLAMA_PREBUILT at all.

Both are now added, conditionally on existing. cc-rs ignores include paths that
do not exist, so covering both shapes costs nothing and stops this file from
encoding a guess about which layout it was handed.

IF NEITHER EXISTS, IT SAYS SO BY NAME

    panic!("no ggml headers under {}: expected ggml/include/ (build tree) or
            ggml-include/ (prebuilt package), found neither. contents: {:?}")

with the directory listing attached. "ggml.h not found" names a header and not a
cause; this names the cause and shows the evidence. Checked before the include()
calls, which take ownership of the paths.

Verified: cargo check -p gs-ffi clean, cargo test --workspace 163 passed / 0 failed.
